text:
Easton Cowan is one of the few Maple Leafs who can say his season is going well. The 21-year-old has eight goals and 17 points in 23 games, and with Kirill Marchenko on injured reserve his ice time has jumped to 19:13 over the last five games from about 15 minutes before.

He brings speed Toronto otherwise lacks: his top skating speed and number of 20 mph bursts rank in the 95th and 96th percentiles. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in nine games, had him as a rush player who carries the puck in and sets up a lot of shots for teammates.

Two cautions. Eight goals on 4.8 expected, shooting 17% against 12% last season, is a finishing rate that rarely lasts. And Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season because opponents got a lot more chances with him on. This year, the Leafs have 51% of the expected goals with him at five on five, better than without him, which on a team that has lost seven straight is a real sign of growth. His goals in the losses to Colorado and Chicago were two of Toronto's few bright moments.
